data.title: SF may soon ban natural gas in homes and businesses undergoing major renovations
data.author: mikhael
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：旧金山燃气设备禁令及其影响

不同观点：
• **反对禁令，支持燃气**：  
  - **SilverElfin**：认为感应炉不如燃气炉 enjoyable，且不能像燃气一样移动锅具保持加热。还提到感应炉对锅具损伤较大。
  - **sugarpimpdorsey**：强调直接燃气的热水器是最简单可靠的设备，不需电力，并指出燃气禁令是“gaslighting”公众，忽视了地震等实际情况。
  
• **支持禁令，认为禁令合理**：  
  - **ZeroGravitas**：认为禁令是合理的政策，指出美国人的观念被扭曲，而在澳大利亚类似政策正在推行。还提到若保留少数用户使用燃气，他们将承担维持燃气网络的全部成本。
  - **archagon**：基于自身经历，提到旧金山许多老旧建筑存在燃气泄漏问题，支持禁令是从公共健康和安全角度出发的合理举措。

• **质疑环保政策的实际效果**：  
  - **johnnienaked**：指出天然气发电厂仍在为旧金山供电，且输电线路引发森林火灾的风险，认为禁令只会使能源成本更高，无法真正减少需求。

• **个人选择与政治因素**：  
  - **whateveracct**：生活在气候政策导向州的背景下，选择购买燃气设备和汽车，认为这是“最后的机会”，反映出对政策变化的个人应对。

• **对住房危机的批评**：  
  - **tlogan**：认为禁令是富裕居民和NIMBYs（"Not In My Backyard"）反对建设新住房的借口，最终只会加剧住房危机，特别是对年轻一代的影响最大。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：  
  - 燃气禁令是否合理及其对公共健康和安全的贡献。  
  - 感应技术的实用性与燃气设备的可靠性对比。  
  - 环保政策是否会导致能源成本上升及对电网的压力。  
  - 燃气禁令与地震等自然灾害应急处理的矛盾。

• **其他值得注意的讨论点**：  
  - 燃气设备禁令对不同社会阶层（如富裕居民与贫困人群）的不同影响。  
  - 政策执行的背景（如旧金山的地理和气候特点）及公众对政策的接受程度。

data.title: Test Results for AMD Zen 5
data.author: matt_d
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AMD处理器的性能、架构设计及其与竞争产品的对比

不同观点：
• **pbsd** 提到，根据AMD Zen 5优化手册，浮点调度器在满载时会有慢速区域，但在特定条件下（如依赖1周期延迟的操作）可能不会受到惩罚。因此，短向量代码在未填满调度器时会有更好的延迟表现。这与通常认为的向量ALU指令延迟为2及更高有所不同。

• **monster_truck** 支持pbsd的观点，认为在充分利用各种优化后，AMD Zen各代处理器仍有剩余的计算能力。他建议使用较少核心以平衡热负载，从而获得更快的性能。

• **kvemkon** 比较了AMD和Apple的处理器，指出即使在缓存大小相似的情况下，AMD在单线程性能上仍有差距。他还提到，与Qualcomm和ARM的处理器相比，AMD需要到Zen 6才能有较大提升。

• **eigenform** 对Zen 3缺少内存重命名但在Zen 4和Zen 5中恢复的现象表示好奇，提出了技术演进的问题。

• **qwertox** 提供了一份关于Intel、AMD和VIA CPU微架构的优化指南链接，供大家参考。

• **kklisura** 询问如何获取所有这些处理器信息，表现出对学习资源的兴趣。

• **ashvardanian** 批评了AMD在AI方面宣传的误导性，指出Zen5与Intel Xeon处理器的实际对比，并怀疑AVX-512支持和核心数量是否足以竞争。

补充讨论：
• **Sesse__, varispeed, alberth, londons_explore** 提供了其他角度的评论，如对测试结果的期待、M4处理器的比较、文章标题的准确性，以及对整数向量指令使用场景的幽默看法。

争议焦点：
• AMD Zen处理器在实际应用中的延迟表现与其文档说明是否一致，以及AMD在市场宣传中是否存在误导。

data.title: Show HN: QuickTunes: Apple Music player for Mac with iPod vibes
data.author: albertru90
data.article_summary: QuickTunes是一款适用于macOS的简洁快速音乐播放器，旨在重现2000年代初iPod的简单音乐播放体验。它支持轻松浏览播放列表、专辑、艺术家和歌曲，并提供流畅的滚动、键盘导航和多点触控手势。应用界面可根据窗口大小动态调整，支持自定义外观。用户可以通过快捷键快速搜索本地或Apple Music曲库，并管理播放队列。其他功能包括使用媒体键控制播放、右键点击Dock图标操作、以及分享当前播放歌曲。兼容macOS 15 "Sequoia"及Apple Silicon和Intel芯片的Mac电脑。提供试用和购买选项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对不同音乐客户端及其功能的讨论，包括对Apple Music及其替代品的评价。

不同观点：
• MBCook认为LongPlay是一个专门为完整专辑播放设计的优秀客户端，强调其专注于专辑播放的独特功能，如按专辑顺序播放和跳过整张专辑的选项。界面展示为专辑封面网格，简洁直观。

• leakycap指出该网站上的传真应用是一个无需订阅即可发送传真的优秀解决方案，虽然与音乐客户端无关，但提供了一种实用的附加功能。

• browningstreet询问是否有适用于Windows的Apple Music替代播放器，指出Windows上的Apple Music应用存在“原生平台应用”的不足之处。

• dontlaugh推荐Cider，一个在Linux上使用的替代音乐播放器，并提供了相关链接，展示了对跨平台解决方案的兴趣。

• eisa01寻求iOS上的Apple Music替代品，表达了对Apple Music应用默认搜索指向Apple Music流媒体服务的不满。

• dangus反驳关于Apple Music应用臃肿的观点，认为Apple已经通过将播客、电视/电影和设备管理移出Apple Music来减少臃肿，并质疑所谓“运行缓慢”的说法，认为这是过时的看法。

• bigyabai提到Spot for Linux，另一个适用于Linux的快捷导向流媒体界面，为放弃Mac的用户提供了另一个选择，并提供了相关链接。

• zapzupnz指出LongPlay的名字与QuickTune非常接近，后者是另一个Apple Music的前端，提醒用户注意两者的相似性和潜在混淆。

• dostick强调现代音乐播放器不仅要关注用户界面和用户体验（UIUX），还要关注支持的音乐存储方式，如DLNA、Plex、Jellyfin等，认为这是用户选择播放器的主要考虑因素。

补充讨论：
• 用户对不同平台（Windows、Linux、iOS）上的Apple Music替代品有各自的需求和推荐，显示出对跨平台解决方案的关注。
• 对Apple Music应用的“臃肿”和性能问题存在争议，部分用户认为其已经过优化，而其他用户则对其功能和默认设置有所不满。
• 支持多种音乐存储和流媒体服务的功能被视为选择音乐播放器的重要因素。

data.title: Asyncio: A library with too many sharp corners
data.author: chubot
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了Python的异步编程库`asyncio`的诸多设计缺陷，认为其存在许多“尖锐的角落”，使用起来非常困难，几乎可以说是有根本性问题。文章指出，尽管`asyncio`在Python 3.4中作为实验性功能引入，并在Python 3.5中正式确立，还引入了`async`和`await`关键字来简化异步编程，但其实现存在许多问题，尤其是与任务取消、I/O操作、以及`asyncio.Queue`相关的部分。

文章列举了`asyncio`的几个主要问题：
1. **取消任务机制存在缺陷**：虽然`asyncio`提供了任务取消功能，但在实际操作中容易导致资源未正确释放。
2. **任务被销毁但仍处于待处理状态**：这会导致难以调试的错误。
3. **I/O操作存在不必要的隐患**：在进行I/O操作时，容易遇到意外错误。
4. **`asyncio.Queue`难以使用**：设计复杂，使用不便。

文章还提到了`Trio`和`AnyIO`库，它们通过实现类似`Trio`的语义，修复了`asyncio`的许多问题，同时保持与`asyncio`库的兼容性。总体而言，文章认为`asyncio`虽然提供了强大的异步编程能力，但其设计和实现存在较多问题，使用时需格外小心。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python中的异步编程（asyncio）及其替代方案（如gevent、Twisted）的优缺点，以及Python语言设计问题。

不同观点：
• **支持gevent**：btown认为gevent通过将所有可能阻塞的操作都打补丁以让位于事件循环，避免了在异步上下文中意外使用同步API的问题，并且不需要为异步和阻塞代码分别实现库，所有代码都能直接工作。他设想了一个Python 4的世界，其中green-threading成为核心特性，而不是像现在这样需要对Django生态系统进行繁琐的重写。

• **批评asyncio**：pansa2批评asyncio有许多设计问题，认为其在实现上不如其他语言的类似库，并指出Python常常在未充分考虑设计和与语言其他部分的兼容性时就急于添加新特性（如asyncio、类型提示和模式匹配）。他认为这种做法导致了Python逐渐偏离了"一种方法做一件事"的哲学。

• **文档问题**：rich_sasha指出asyncio的文档不够全面，虽然有教程式的介绍，但重要细节常常被忽略，需要在评论或非官方资源（如Reddit和StackExchange）中寻找。

• **Python整体问题**：mikert89认为Python在项目初期表现良好，但在项目后期会遇到问题，常常希望重写为Java。Philpax和drkrab也认为Python在并发编程方面存在根本性的 quirky 设计问题。

• **Twisted的支持**：lormayna和dade_认为Twisted比asyncio更可用，尽管asyncio已有改进，但仍希望Python能引入类似Go的协程、waitgroups和channels的机制。dade_更是直接表示Twisted更胜一筹。

补充讨论：
• **AnyIO的推荐**：dagenix建议使用AnyIO，这是一个构建在asyncio之上的接口，解决了asyncio的许多缺点。

• **对取消操作的争议**：bsder回应了关于线程取消的讨论，指出传统线程模型中没有干净的取消方式，Java对stop()的弃用是有理由的。o11c和anal_reactor则对取消操作提出了技术性和哲学性的质疑，认为取消在某些情况下可能是不合理的。

争议焦点：
• asyncio的设计和实现是否合理，特别是其取消操作和整体复杂性。

44697761.article_content:
asyncio: a library with too many sharp corners
28/03/2025 17:39:22
A red garden tulip. Photo
by my friend Jamie.
One of the headliner features of Python 3.4 (released in 2014) was a new library in the standard
library:
asyncio
, provisionally introduced for feedback as an import of the
external
tulip
library. In Python 3.5 (released in 2015),
async
and
await
were added as keywords to the language specifically for usage with
asynchronous libraries, replacing the usage of
yield from
. The
asyncio
module was also made non-provisional in this release, heralding an entire
new ecosystem of asynchronous libraries in the Python world.
But
asyncio
has so many sharp corners and design issues it is far too difficult to
use, bordering on being fundamentally broken. Some of these were only realised in hindsight
because other languages (Kotlin, Swift) and libraries did what
asyncio
does
significantly better; but most of these issues were bad at release and it is baffling how the
library made it out of provisional status with such glaring flaws.
I mention the
Trio
library a lot in this
post, but there's also the
AnyIO
library that implements
Trio-like semantics on top of
asyncio
, fixing most of the issues described here
whilst retaining a level of compatibility with regular
asyncio
libraries.
Contents
Major Problem #1: Cancellation is broken
Major Problem #2: Task was destroyed but it is pending!
Major Problem #3: I/O has pointless landmines
Major Problem #4:
asyncio.Queue
is difficult to use
Other, less major problems
Major Problem #1: Cancellation is broken
In the traditional model of concurrent programming using threads, there is no clean way to do
cancellation. In the standard
pthreads
model, the only way to do cancellation is to
brutally murder a thread using
pthread_kill
, which is nearly always a bad idea
because anything the thread was using (such as locks) will be in an unknown and inconsistent
state if the thread was killed in the middle of an operation. If you want a better mechanism,
you need to implement it yourself by constantly polling a shared state object in-between doing
work, using a loop like so:
cancelled = threading.Event()
def t1():
while not cancelled.is_set():
do_work()
def main():
threading.Thread(target=t1).start()
# ... do something inbetween
cancelled.set()
This is unergonomic and error-prone as only threads that opt-in to this cancellation mechanism
can be cancelled and only when they explicitly check if they are cancelled. Some languages (i.e.
Java) make this a bit better by having a
Thread.interrupt()
method that handles
dealing with communicating the interrupted state, with most standard library functions such as
Object.wait()
automatically checking for the interrupted state. (This still falls
victim to the other issues described here.)
asyncio
is an asynchronous runtime and is responsible for its own scheduling of its
own tasks, instead of the kernel. When an
asyncio
task needs to interact with the
system, it asks the event loop to suspend it until an operation is complete whereupon the task
will be rescheduled and will run again in the next tick of the event loop. Threads do the same,
but with system calls, and the user application has no control over the kernel's scheduler
beyond tweaking some tuning parameters.
This scheduling mechanism is reused to implement cancellation. When a task is cancelled, any
pending operation that the event loop was performing for a task is cancelled, and instead the
call raises a
CancelledError
. Unlike threads tasks no longer need to check if they
have been cancelled; every single time a call drops into the event loop the runtime itself
checks for cancellation. Conceptually, you can imagine every
await
as a
cancellation point
:
async def something(stream: SomeLibraryStream):
while True:
result = await stream.read()  # Cancellation point
parsed = do_parse(result)     # *not* a cancellation point
From this, we can derive a conceptual model of how tasks and cancellations interact:
Tasks run until an
await
, at which point they suspend.
Something else calls
task.cancel()
, which reschedules the task again.
The function that was being
await
-ed now raises
Cancelled
.
This exception propagates backwards, unwinding through all functions in the call stack and
cleaning up as it goes.
This avoids both problems with threads: tasks can be externally killed without worrying about
resources not being torn down, and end-user tasks don't need to constantly check if they've been
cancelled because the event loop does it for you.
But that's not how it works
Consider this function below that returns a resource wrapped in an asynchronous context manager.
When the user is done, it needs to clean up some resources (say, a server needs a clean close).
This cleanup should be done regardless of if the code running inside the context manager was
successful or not, so it's ran inside a
finally
block:
@asynccontextmanager
async def connect_to_server(ip: str, *, port: int = 6767) -> A
44697761.article_summary:
文章讨论了Python的异步编程库`asyncio`的诸多设计缺陷，认为其存在许多“尖锐的角落”，使用起来非常困难，几乎可以说是有根本性问题。文章指出，尽管`asyncio`在Python 3.4中作为实验性功能引入，并在Python 3.5中正式确立，还引入了`async`和`await`关键字来简化异步编程，但其实现存在许多问题，尤其是与任务取消、I/O操作、以及`asyncio.Queue`相关的部分。

文章列举了`asyncio`的几个主要问题：
1. **取消任务机制存在缺陷**：虽然`asyncio`提供了任务取消功能，但在实际操作中容易导致资源未正确释放。
2. **任务被销毁但仍处于待处理状态**：这会导致难以调试的错误。
3. **I/O操作存在不必要的隐患**：在进行I/O操作时，容易遇到意外错误。
4. **`asyncio.Queue`难以使用**：设计复杂，使用不便。

文章还提到了`Trio`和`AnyIO`库，它们通过实现类似`Trio`的语义，修复了`asyncio`的许多问题，同时保持与`asyncio`库的兼容性。总体而言，文章认为`asyncio`虽然提供了强大的异步编程能力，但其设计和实现存在较多问题，使用时需格外小心。

data.author: virgildotcodes
data.article_summary: 文章提出了一种利用太阳辐射进行星际探测的新方法——太阳辐射扭矩加速器（TARS）。该系统通过两个对比反照率的薄表面，在靠近太阳的准卫星轨道上逐渐旋转加速，将太阳能转化为旋转动能，最终释放以推动微型探测器达到星际速度。利用商用材料（如碳纳米管片），手机大小的探测器可在一年内实现星际飞行，系统总重约一公斤。尽管理论上速度无上限，但实际设计中速度提升会导致系统尺寸指数级增长，使得相对论速度不切实际。通过使用石墨烯片、引力辅助等策略可进一步提升速度，为高功率定向能系统不实用时提供了一种低成本的亚相对论性星际探测方案。

不同观点：
• [xerox13ster] 认为“TAURUS”这个替代名称更符合语法，且包含更多有用信息，批评原命名为了模仿科幻机器人名字而显得生硬和不实用。
• [EndsOfnversion] 对TARS概念感兴趣，但质疑其技术可行性，指出在如此长时间的高重力加速度下，任何有效载荷是否能够存活，并用子弹出膛时的加速度作类比。
• [bad_username] 对技术细节提出疑问，质疑在TARS处于圆形轨道时，为何载荷释放不需要精确计时，并指出在同一平面内仍有360度的自由度，且对如何在极端辐射和高速旋转下保持计时器精确性表示怀疑。

值得注意的细节：
• 不同评论者从命名、物理可行性、工程技术等多个角度对TARS进行剖析，展现了对该概念的多维度思考。

Title:
Torqued Accelerator using Radiation from the Sun (TARS) for Interstellar Payloads
Authors:
David Kipping
,
Kathryn Lampo
View a PDF of the paper titled Torqued Accelerator using Radiation from the Sun (TARS) for Interstellar Payloads, by David Kipping and Kathryn Lampo
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
The concept of exploring space using solar power is energetically appealing, but interstellar solar sails typically require extremely low areal densities (~0.8 g/m^2). This work explores an alternative approach: storing solar energy as rotational kinetic energy, which is later released to propel a microprobe beyond the solar system. The proposed Torqued Accelerator using Radiation from the Sun (TARS) consists of two thin surfaces with contrasting albedos that gradually spins up over weeks to months while in a sub-Keplerian "quasite" orbit around the Sun. Though constrained by material strengths, careful design allows a phone-sized payload to reach interstellar velocities in less than a year, using commercially available materials (e.g. CNT sheets). The entire system spans tens of meters and weighs of order of a kilogram. Whilst there is no theoretical limit to the achievable speeds, practical designs grow exponentially in size as velocity targets increase, making interstellar flight feasible but relativistic speeds implausible. Several strategies, including the use of graphene sheets, gravity assists, the Oberth effect, and electrostatic confinement, could further maximise velocity. TARS is an attractive light sail technology when high-powered directed energy systems are impractical, offering a potentially low-cost solution for deploying small, sub-relativistic interstellar probes.

data.title: Teach Yourself Programming in Ten Years (1998)
data.author: smartmic
data.article_summary: Peter Norvig的文章《Teach Yourself Programming in Ten Years》批评了速成编程书籍的流行，如《24小时学会Java》等。他指出，编程是一项需要长时间学习和实践的技能，不可能在短时间内掌握。研究表明，要在任何领域达到专家水平，通常需要十年或约10,000小时的刻意练习。速成课程只能提供表面的知识，无法让人深入理解和掌握编程。Norvig引用多位专家和历史人物的观点，强调真正的专业技能需要一生的努力，速成法并不实际。他建议学习者要有耐心，通过持续的挑战和反思来提高编程能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“短时间内自学编程”的可行性及相关资源（书籍、文章、编程语言等）的讨论。

不同观点：
• II2II认为，这些号称短时间内能教授编程的书籍不应被轻易否定。它们为初学者提供了进一步学习的基础，并且以友好的方式介绍编程，避免让初学者感到畏惧。这些书籍将学习内容分成24个一小时的模块，能够合理覆盖编程语言的基础知识。不过，有些书籍的问题在于写得不好，而不是概念本身有误。
• neilv引用了Peter Norvig的文章《Teach Yourself Programming in Ten Years》，认为短时间内学会编程是不现实的。Norvig的文章广泛分享和讨论，并被翻译成20多种语言。如果按照这篇文章的观点，那些花时间在短期学习上的人可能会失去进入Google等公司工作的机会，因为他们没有为面试做好准备。
• jaimebuelta指出，阅读标为1998年的文章却包含较新的内容（如电影《Ratatouile》）让人感到困惑。文章推荐了一些1998年合适的编程语言（如C++）却又推荐了Go语言，这种混搭让人感到怪异。
• WillAdams讨论了是否有机制可以显著简化编程学习，并提到了BASIC和C语言的局限性。他还引用了Brooks的《No Silver Bullets》一文，并询问Swift和SwiftUI是否改变了这种计算方式。
• aizk作为一个年轻的开发者，对Google Groups和Usenet的历史感到陌生，并将Usenet比作90年代至2000年代的论坛，询问Discord是否是当代等价物。
• la_fayette好奇Norvig对LLMs（大型语言模型）在编程中应用的看法。

补充讨论：
• coldcode和intellectronica分享了他们多年编程经验，强调编程是一个持续学习的过程。
• 多次提及Norvig的文章《Teach Yourself Programming in Ten Years》在不同年份的讨论链接，显示出该话题的长期关注度。

44697007.article_content:
Teach Yourself Programming in Ten Years
Peter Norvig
Why is everyone in such a rush?
Walk into any bookstore, and you'll see how to
Teach Yourself Java
in 24 Hours
alongside endless variations offering to teach C,
SQL, Ruby, Algorithms, and so on in a few days or hours.
The Amazon advanced search for [
title: teach,
yourself, hours, since: 2000
and found 512 such books. Of the top ten, nine are programming books (the other is about bookkeeping). Similar results come from replacing "teach yourself" with "learn" or "hours" with "days."
The conclusion is that either people are in a big rush to learn
about programming, or that programming is somehow fabulously easier to
learn than anything else.
Felleisen
et al.
give a nod to this trend in their book
How to Design Programs
, when they say
"Bad programming is easy.
Idiots
can learn it in
21 days
,
even if they are
dummies
." The Abtruse Goose comic also had
their take
.
Let's analyze what a title like
Teach Yourself C++ in 24 Hours
could mean:
Teach Yourself:
In 24 hours you won't have time to write several
significant programs, and learn from your successes and failures with
them.  You won't have time to work with an experienced programmer and
understand what it is like to live in a C++ environment.  In short, you
won't have time to learn much.  So the book can only be talking about a
superficial familiarity, not a deep understanding. As Alexander Pope said,
a little learning is a dangerous thing.
C++:
In 24 hours you might be able to learn some of the syntax of
C++ (if you already know another language), but you couldn't
learn much about how to use the language.  In short, if you were, say, a
Basic programmer, you could learn to write programs in the style of
Basic using C++ syntax, but you couldn't learn what C++ is
actually good (and bad) for.  So what's the point?
Alan
Perlis
once said: "A language that doesn't affect the way you
think about programming, is not worth knowing".  One possible point is
that you have to learn a tiny bit of C++ (or more likely, something
like JavaScript or Processing) because you need to interface with an
existing tool to accomplish a specific task. But then you're not
learning how to program; you're learning to accomplish that task.
in 24 Hours:
Unfortunately, this is not enough, as the next
section shows.
Teach Yourself Programming in Ten Years
Researchers (
Bloom
(1985)
,
Bryan & Harter (1899)
,
Hayes
(1989)
,
Simmon & Chase (1973)
) have shown it
takes about ten years to develop expertise in any of a wide variety of
areas, including chess playing, music composition, telegraph
operation, painting, piano playing, swimming, tennis, and research in
neuropsychology and topology.  The key is
deliberative
practice: not just doing it again and again, but challenging yourself
with a task that is just beyond your current ability, trying it,
analyzing your performance while and after doing it, and correcting
any mistakes.  Then repeat.  And repeat again.  There appear to be no
real shortcuts: even Mozart, who was a musical prodigy at age 4, took
13 more years before he began to produce world-class music.  In
another genre, the Beatles seemed to burst onto the scene with a
string of #1 hits and an appearance on the Ed Sullivan show in 1964.
But they had been playing small clubs in Liverpool and Hamburg since
1957, and while they had mass appeal early on, their first great
critical success,
Sgt. Peppers
, was released in 1967.
Malcolm
Gladwell
has popularized the idea, although he concentrates on 10,000 hours, not 10 years.
Henri Cartier-Bresson (1908-2004) had another metric: "Your first 10,000 photographs are your  worst." (He didn't
anticipate that with digital cameras, some people can reach that mark in a week.)
True expertise may take a lifetime:
Samuel Johnson (1709-1784) said "Excellence in any department can be
attained only by the labor of a lifetime; it is not to be purchased at
a lesser price."  And Chaucer (1340-1400) complained "the lyf so short, the craft
so long to lerne." Hippocrates (c. 400BC) is known for the excerpt "ars longa,
vita brevis", which is part of the longer quotation "Ars longa, vita
brevis, occasio praeceps, experimentum periculosum, iudicium
difficile", which in English renders as "Life is short, [the] craft
long, opportunity fleeting, experiment treacherous, judgment
difficult."
Of course, no single number can be the final answer: it doesn't seem reasonable
to assume that all skills (e.g., programming, chess playing, checkers playing, and music playing)
could all require exactly the same amount of time to master, nor that all people
will take exactly the same amount of time. As
Prof.
K. Anders Ericsson
puts it, "In most domains it's remarkable how much time even the most
talented individuals need in order to reach the highest levels of performance. The 10,000 hour number just gives you a sense that we're talking years of 10 to 20 hours a week which those who some people would argue are the most innately
44697007.article_summary: Peter Norvig的文章《Teach Yourself Programming in Ten Years》批评了速成编程书籍的流行，如《24小时学会Java》等。他指出，编程是一项需要长时间学习和实践的技能，不可能在短时间内掌握。研究表明，要在任何领域达到专家水平，通常需要十年或约10,000小时的刻意练习。速成课程只能提供表面的知识，无法让人深入理解和掌握编程。Norvig引用多位专家和历史人物的观点，强调真正的专业技能需要一生的努力，速成法并不实际。他建议学习者要有耐心，通过持续的挑战和反思来提高编程能力。

• II2II认为，这些号称短时间内能教授编程的书籍不应被轻易否定。它们为初学者提供了进一步学习的基础，并且以友好的方式介绍编程，避免让初学者感到畏惧。这些书籍将学习内容分成24个一小时的模块，能够合理覆盖编程语言的基础知识。不过，有些书籍的问题在于写得不好，而不是概念本身有误。
• neilv引用了Peter Norvig的文章《Teach Yourself Programming in Ten Years》，认为短时间内学会编程是不现实的。Norvig的文章广泛分享和讨论，并被翻译成20多种语言。如果按照这篇文章的观点，那些花时间在短期学习上的人可能会失去进入Google等公司工作的机会，因为他们没有为面试做好准备。

data.title: Visualizing TCP
data.author: waaldev
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了通过可视化方式理解TCP和排序算法。作者Russ Cox分享了一个视频，该视频通过将数据包表现为在客户端和服务器之间飞行的球体，以比实际时间慢40倍的速度展示了HTTP GET过程，帮助直观理解TCP会话。作者联想到排序算法的可视化，提到Aldo Cortesi的博客，指出时间动画难以回答与时间相关的问题，建议使用静态图形展示数组元素随时间变化的路径。受此启发，作者通过工具生成TCP交互的静态图形，发现这种方法有助于仔细研究异常和识别模式。例如，图形展示了TCP三次握手、客户端延迟ACK策略以及服务器窗口大小变化等细节。这种静态图形方式比动画更易于分析和理解网络交互过程。

44697217.article_content:
research!rsc
Thoughts and links about programming,
by
Russ Cox
RSS
Visualizing TCP
Posted on Monday, December 13, 2010.
This video
depicts an HTTP GET by showing
packets as balls flying between client and server, slowed 40x compared to real time.
It's pretty nice for getting a visceral sense of the underlying TCP session:
you can see individual rounds at the start and then as the session stabilizes the rounds begin to overlap enough that they disappear.
When I saw the video, it reminded me of the ever-present videos of sorting algorithms,
like the ones on the Wikipedia
heapsort
and
quicksort
pages:
That in turn reminded me of a 2007 blog post
by Aldo Cortesi about
visualizing sorting algorithms
using graphs instead of videos.  He points out that the animations make time-based questions difficult to answer:
[It] is my measured opinion that this animation has all the explanatory power of a glob of porridge flung against a wall. To see why I say this, try to find rough answers to the following set of simple questions with reference to it:
After what percentage of time is half of the array sorted?
Can you find an element that moved about half the length of the array to reach its final destination?
What percentage of the array was sorted after 80% of the sorting process? How about 20%?
Does the number of sorted elements grow linearly or non-linearly with time (i.e. logarithmically or exponentially)?
If you thought that was harder than it needed to be, blame animation. First, while humans are great at estimating distances in space, they are pretty bad at estimating distances in time. This is why you had to watch the animation two or three times to answer the first question. When we translate time to a geometric length, as is done in any scientific diagram with a time dimension, this estimation process becomes easy. Second, many questions about sorting algorithms require us to actively compare the sorting state at two or more different time points. Since we don't have perfect memories, this is very, very hard in all but the simplest cases. This leaves us with a strangely one-dimensional view into an animation - we can see what's on screen at any given moment, but we have to strain to answer simple questions about, say, rates of change. Which is why the final question is hard to answer accurately.
Instead, he suggests plotting static graphs showing the paths of
individual array elements over time.
Here are his original visualizations of heapsort and quicksort:
The blog post is worth reading in full.  It has much more detail and links to many other interesting blog posts and a new site dedicated to those visualizations,
sortvis.org
.
Remembering this made me wonder if the lesson of the sorting
animations applied to the TCP animations too, so I collected my
own tcpdumps of both sides of an HTTP GET, pulled out the
trusty (but neglected) Unix tool
join
(1)
to produce a dump with two timestamps on each packet,
and then used Perl to turn it into a graph (
raw PostScript
):
Time marches to the right, with each row picking up where
the previous one left off.  Blue lines indicate packets from
the client and black lines indicate packets from the server.
I think this kind of graph has the same important benefits that
Cortesi realized with his sorting graphs.  It's static, so you
have time to study it, focus on anomalies, or notice patterns
that aren't immediately apparent.  The geometry of the lines,
with flatter slopes corresponding to slower packets, makes it
easy to compare speeds.
Here are just a few things I noticed.
The connection starts with the usual 3-way TCP handshake.
The client sends the third packet in the handshake and
the first data packet back to back, one of its few back-to-back
transmissions.  After the handshake and the initial GET,
which probably fits entirely in that first packet, the client
only receives data: the black lines are large payloads
while the blue lines are ACK messages that trigger more
payloads.
Scanning across the client's view of the connection
(the top edge of each row) we can see that the client
is using the standard delayed ACKs, sending an ACK every two packets.
Scanning across the server's view of the connection
(the bottom edge of each row) we can see that the
server usually responds to the acknowledgement of
two packets by sending two more packets, leaving
the TCP window size (the number of packets in flight) unchanged.
Occasionally, though, the server grows the window size
by responding with three packets instead of two.
Three of these events are circled in rows 1 and 2.
Occasionally the server only responds to an ACK with
a single packet, but most of those appear to be times when
the client was only acknowledging a single packet.
We can count the number of packets in flight at any
given time by counting the number of black lines that
cross a particular blue line, plus the number of packets
sent when the blue line reaches the server.

data.title: Write "Freehold" Software
data.author: rjinman
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于"freehold软件"的定义、适用性及其与当前软件商业模式（如订阅制和微交易）的对比和讨论。

不同观点：
• **tenacious_tuna** 认为，作者在讨论"freehold软件"时引用ChatGPT定义显得有些不一致，因为ChatGPT和类似的托管大语言模型与"freehold软件"的概念相悖。他对文章中的轶事部分也表示困惑，不确定其意义何在。

• **Paradigm2020** 指出，当前"freehold软件"的分类标准过于严格，导致一些价格合理且优质的游戏被排除在外。例如，《Polytopia》因为包含微交易而不被视为"freehold软件"，但这些微交易类似于过去的扩展包，如《星际争霸II》的扩展包。他还提到，不应将开发者与市场平台混为一谈，否则会导致类似"亚马逊基础"系列的问题。

• **ktallett** 完全赞同"freehold软件"的原则，并表示自己发布的任何作品都遵循这一原则。然而，他对如何让更多软件回归这种模式表示怀疑。他提到，目前成功的"freehold软件"例子包括Goodnotes和Affinity设计应用，而这些应用通过重大更新来节省重复购买是可接受的。他还指出，许多人可能更倾向于订阅制，因为社会消费习惯发生了变化，许多人不愿意为软件支付显著的前期费用。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：对于"freehold软件"的定义和分类标准存在争议。Paradigm2020认为当前标准过于严格，而ktallett则关注如何让更多软件回归这种模式。

• **微交易和扩展包的类比**：Paradigm2020提出微交易与传统扩展包的相似性，质疑对"freehold软件"的严格分类。

• **社会消费习惯的变化**：ktallett提到，现代消费者更倾向于小额持续支付（如订阅制），而不愿支付高额前期费用，这对传统"freehold软件"模式提出了挑战。

• **ChatGPT的相关性**：tenacious_tuna对ChatGPT在讨论中的引用提出质疑，认为其与"freehold软件"概念不符，反映出对讨论主题一致性的关注。

data.title: Low cost mmWave 60GHz radar sensor for advanced sensing
data.author: teleforce
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了BGT60TR13C雷达传感器的主要特性及其应用。该传感器工作在60GHz频段，内置天线，采用Finite-State Machine（FSM）管理频率调制和数据采集，通过SPI接口进行配置和控制。其特点包括高信噪比、高带宽、低功耗以及小尺寸（6.5 x 5.0 x 0.9 mm³）。应用场景广泛，涵盖消费电子、无人机、智能家居、安防系统和智能温控等领域。此外，文中还提供了技术支持和设计资源的获取途径。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：毫米波雷达传感器的技术特性、应用场景及其局限性

不同观点：
• Animats认为该设备为爱好者提供了丰富的功能，如蓝牙、WiFi连接和Android应用，且兼容一些Adafruit产品，这在IC数据表中不常见。然而，其角度分辨率为20度，距离分辨率为1米，且只能检测固定物体，范围仅10米。对于只需简单动作检测的场景（如开灯），有更便宜的微波探测器可选。

• Catbert59提到中国Hi-Link提供的50GHz到60GHz的雷达模块，价格在10-30€，易于在固件和PCB层面进行逆向工程。其中一些是连续波雷达，少数是FMCW雷达，使用Infineon 60GHz雷达芯片，且无需签署NDA即可获取工具和数据表。此外，提到ICLink的ICL1122/ICL1112雷达IC，价格约10€，但数据表难找。

• Scoreandmore分享了使用KIT-CSK-BGT60TR13C制作汽车检测器的经验，认为该设备配置简单且有趣，但发现类似创意早已存在。

data.title: Smallest particulate matter air quality sensor for ultra-compact IoT devices
data.author: Liftyee
data.article_summary: Bosch Sensortec在CES上推出了全球最小的颗粒物（PM2.5）传感器BMV080，体积比同类产品小450倍，具有无噪音、无风扇和免维护的特点。该传感器能够精准测量PM2.5浓度，提供实时、可操作的空气质量数据，特别适用于室内环境监测。其创新设计无需风扇，避免了灰尘积累，适合集成于可穿戴设备和物联网设备中，如空气质量监测器、智能恒温器和智能音箱等。BMV080帮助识别和应对不良空气质量，提升健康和福祉。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：无风扇颗粒物传感器的工作原理、应用场景、技术细节及其实用性

不同观点：
• [技术原理] **zevon** 对无风扇传感器的工作原理表示好奇，认为主要区别在于软件和算法，而非硬件。
• [技术对比] **pppone** 提到自己使用的Sensirion SPS30传感器表现良好，并对Bosch传感器的维护需求提出疑问。
• [环境影响] **Catbert59** 指出许多传感器在雾天或霾天表现不佳，并询问新模型如何应对这种情况，提出了通过计算露点来改善数据质量的现有解决方案。

补充讨论：
• [应用场景] **benbojangles** 质疑微型颗粒物传感器的实际应用，特别是是否会集成到智能手机或手表中，并讨论了其潜在用途。
• [社会意义] **alliao** 对技术进步与公共空间空气过滤的政治争议之间的关系发表了看法，表达了对未来清洁空气的期望。

技术细节：
• [尺寸与设计] **smingo** 提供了传感器尺寸细节，并提到它使用激光和透镜，通过光电二极管和算法来计数颗粒物，同时指出需要散热片。
• [尺寸误导性] **progbits** 认为尺寸宣传有误导性，因为用户仍需自行添加金属外壳和透镜，增加了整体尺寸，尤其对DIY爱好者不友好，期待更集成的小型模块。

实用性与可靠性：
• [空气流动影响] **TimByte** 对无风扇设计的可靠性表示关注，特别是在实际环境中如何应对空气流动变化。
• [消费电子集成] **arnejenssen** 期待将这种传感器集成到手机或手表中，用于空气质量监测。
• [消费电子现状] **dzhiurgis** 希望MacBook内置空气传感器，因为已经有风扇，可以实现连续监测。

争议与信任：
• [信任问题] **ck2** 表示除非有AirGradient和BreatheSafeAir.com的技术对比，否则不会完全信任这种新传感器。

其他：
• [文字澄清] **SideburnsOfDoom** 对评论中的语法歧义进行了澄清，指出传感器是“最小尺寸的颗粒物传感器”，而非“测量最小颗粒物的传感器”。

总结：评论围绕传感器的工作原理、技术细节、应用场景及其实际可靠性展开讨论，部分用户关注其在消费电子产品中的潜在应用，而其他用户则对其技术细节和数据可靠性提出质疑。

44698733.article_content:
World's smallest particulate matter sensor revolutionizes air quality measurement
Noiseless, fanless, and maintenance-free sensor provides accurate data
Learn more about BMV080
Worldâs smallest particulate matter (PM2.5) air quality sensor (450 times smaller in volume than alternatives) enabling use in ultra-compact IoT devices
Accurate measurement of PM2.5 concentration providing actionable data
Innovative fanless design is silent and maintenance-free
Bosch at CES: booth 16115 and start of new #LikeABosch campaign
Clean air is fundamental to our health and well-being. Today, people typically spend approximately 90% of their time indoors, which has a negative long-term impact on health because indoor air is three to five times more polluted than in the outdoor environment in most parts of the world. A major component of this pollution is fine dust known as PM2.5 particulates, which are solid and liquid particles smaller than 2.5 Î¼m. These particulates are inhaled and enter the lungs, where they cause serious health problems.
The most common air quality measurement stations only provide outdoor data averaged over time, which fails to deliver real-time, localized information most relevant to our health. At CESÂ® in Las Vegas, Nevada, Bosch Sensortec is addressing this issue with its new BMV080, the worldâs smallest PM2.5 air quality sensor, which provides accurate, actionable data.
âIndoor air quality is a problem: in poorly ventilated homes, PM2.5 concentration from domestic cooking can reach levels 100 times higher than acceptable limits,â said Dr. Lucas Ginzinger, Head of Product Area Optics at Bosch Sensortec. âWith localized, actionable data from the new BMV080, itâs now possible to identify and respond to poor air quality.â
The BMV080 utilizes an innovative design based on ultra-compact lasers with integrated photodiodes.
"The BMV080 provides timely, accurate and actionable information about particulate concentration levels in the air, enabling the identification and handling of indoor and outdoor pollution to improve people's well-being and health."
Dr. Stefan Finkbeiner, CEO at Bosch Sensortec
The BMV080 sensing element measures only 4.2 x 3.5 x 3 mmÂ³ (W x L x H), which is more than 450 times smaller in volume than any comparable device on the market. The miniscule size and fanless, non-intrusive design of the BMV080 are a game-changer, and its noiseless operation means it does not disturb residents who may be sleeping or working.
The new sensor is maintenance-free with no fan-induced dust buildup, which means that itâs more reliable, and less prone to malfunction. It is a natural fit for ultra-compact wearable or IoT devices such as air quality monitors, smart thermostats, smart speakers, smart switches and smart air purifiers.
Click through example applications:
Facing a lot of damaging pollutants in the air is usual, especially in a subway station. The BMV080 in wearables measures air quality and assists on when to use a mask for health protection.
Certain cooking styles like frying or roasting release particulates that can lead to adverse health consequences. The BMV080 knows exactly when and at what stage ventilation needs to be activated.
Relaxing next to a fireplace might sound comforting. However, wood burning produces particulates damaging to our health. The BMV080 detects these and can trigger air purifiers in the right mode.
/
Comparable state-of-the-art PM2.5 sensors all rely on a fan to draw air across a laser beam, where a photodiode then detects and measures the particulates as they reflect or block the light from the laser. The BMV080 utilizes an innovative design based on ultra-compact lasers with integrated photodiodes. It applies sophisticated algorithms to measure the PM2.5 concentration directly in free space, without requiring a fan.
450 times smaller
in volume than any comparable device on the market.
The innovation brings awareness and choice to people who value healthy living. The new sensor is easily integrated into ultra-compact IoT-based smart home and smart building systems to deliver air quality notifications to residents when PM2.5 levels rise above a threshold level. To take action, the resident or home automation system can ventilate by switching on an exhaust fan or filter to clear the air.
"The BMV080 provides timely, accurate and actionable information about particulate concentration levels in the air, enabling the identification and handling of indoor and outdoor pollution to improve people's well-being and health,â said Stefan Finkbeiner, CEO at Bosch Sensortec. "It is dramatically smaller than existing devices on the market and opens up an entirely new set of applications for design engineers to explore."

data.title: Chemical process produces critical battery metals with no waste
data.author: stubish
data.article_summary: Aspiring Minerals，一家位于新西兰的公司，正在运营一个试点工厂，将橄榄石分解为多种有价值的材料。其化学工艺可以从橄榄石中提取关键电池金属，如镍和钴，且整个过程几乎不产生废物。该技术不仅提高了资源利用率，还减少了传统采矿和冶炼过程对环境的影响。这一创新有助于满足全球对电池金属日益增长的需求，同时推动可持续发展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： Olivine矿物的应用、提取技术及其经济与环境影响

不同观点：
• **Kragen**：Kragen认为橄榄石在高温下稳定，适合用于铸造，且由于其与CO₂的反应特性，曾被提议用于逆转全球变暖。然而，开采地幔中的橄榄石面临巨大的技术挑战。他还提到橄榄石中的镍和钴杂质使其成为这些金属的经济来源。
• **Kurthr**：Kurthr指出，许多稀有金属是其他矿石加工的副产品，例如硒、钴来自铜矿，铟、锗、镓来自锌矿等。这种依赖关系可能导致副产品的需求超过主产品的需求，从而导致价格上涨。
• **Bruce511**：Bruce511对机械技术的实际应用持谨慎乐观态度，认为很多 hype 可能最终无疾而终。他希望这个项目能够从试验工厂阶段走向全面生产。
• **Schobi**：Schobi关注橄榄石提取工艺的细节，包括当前工厂的生产能力、生产批次的时间、混合金属产品的纯度和比例，以及整体经济效益。他质疑该工艺是否只是更环保但更昂贵的提取方法，还是会取代其他污染严重的采矿方法。
• **Phtrivier**：Phtrivier关心的是从传统来源和“回收”版本中获取NMC的成本，并希望获得更多价格信息。
• **Hinkley**：Hinkley关注工艺的优化，特别是如何通过并行反应链缩短生产时间，并提到工人班次对硬件利用率的影响。
• **Mikewarot**：Mikewarot认为该工艺可以很好地结合间歇性能源输入，如太阳能或风能，从而提高能源效率。
• **Idontwantthis**：Idontwantthis认为该工艺可以用于碳捕集与封存，赋予橄榄石新的价值，同时产生可用于捕获CO₂的橄榄石粉尘。
• **GreenSalem**：GreenSalem对澳大利亚公司在获取政府资助后失败的历史表示担忧，指出这些公司常因实施不力、质量控制差和缺乏专业人员而倒闭。同时，他认为中国在技术研究和转化方面做得更好。

补充讨论：
• 工艺的经济效益与环境影响之间的平衡是讨论的核心。
• 橄榄石作为金属来源的潜力及其与其他矿物提取工艺的关系也被广泛讨论。
• 技术优化和生产效率提升是多个评论关注的细节。
• 不同评论者对该技术实际应用的前景持不同态度，从乐观到谨慎甚至怀疑。

Laurie Winkless

Aspiring Minerals

data.title: Fast and cheap bulk storage: using LVM to cache HDDs on SSDs
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何利用Linux的逻辑卷管理器（LVM）构建一个缓存的RAID阵列，结合SSD和HDD以实现高性价比的存储方案。SSD用于加速频繁访问数据的读取，而大容量的HDD用于存储不常访问的数据。作者选择LVM缓存而不是ZFS或其他工具，因为LVM配置简单且兼容性好。HDD部分采用RAID 1以提高数据可靠性，防止磁盘故障导致数据丢失。文章详细介绍了硬件设置、RAID 1配置、缓存分区创建及逻辑卷管理的具体步骤，并讨论了该方案的优势和注意事项。通过这种方式，用户可以在享受SSD高速性能的同时，利用HDD的大容量存储。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LVM和RAID的使用经验与技术选择

不同观点：
• [oakwhiz] 认为LVM与RAID的组合（如RAID1和RAID5）在设置上复杂且容易出问题，但设置完成后运行良好。他指出不同RAID级别（RAID0、RAID1、RAID5）可根据需求应用于不同卷。
• [dale_glass] 强调LVM的功能被低估，建议将所有硬盘放入同一个卷组（VG）而不是使用RAID，然后可以在逻辑卷（LV）上应用不同RAID级别。他还提到LVM的其他高级功能如缓存、快照和精简配置，但警告精简配置可能引发问题。
• [gopalv] 分享了使用SSD缓存ext4日志的经验，指出缓存可以提升性能，但SSD故障可能导致数据丢失。他还提到HDFS对RAID的需求不同于传统系统。
• [Szpadel] 指出RAID1仅保护硬盘的灾难性故障，无法防止数据损坏。相比之下，ZFS和Btrfs通过校验和提供更高的数据完整性保护。
• [KaiserPro] 对mdadm和LVM持批评态度，认为文档质量差且LVM快照功能曾有问题。他推荐ZFS或GPFS作为替代方案。
• [riedel] 询问QNAP NAS的自动分层技术，并表示对灵活分层而非缓存的兴趣。

补充讨论：
• [thebeardisred] 指出需要通过测试工具（如fio、rsync）定量评估性能改进。
• [jpecar] 提到自2017年以来使用LVM缓存的经验，但由于缓存行为不符合工作负载需求而最终转向全闪存。
• [bjt12345] 怀念Optane驱动器。
• [rsync] 提到ZFS的元数据缓存设备功能，可以显著提升IOPS。
• [hinkley] 提到将数据库的WAL文件放在最快存储上以加速数据库。
• [whazor] 建议使用三个驱动器时，用一个驱动器进行写回以提高写速度。
• [sneak] 采用在SSD上存储数据并连续备份到HDD的策略，以实现快速且便宜的数据存储。
• [iam-TJ] 分享了复杂的LVM和RAID组合设置经验，包括使用LUKS加密和iSCSI进行远程备份与恢复。

争议焦点：
• LVM和RAID的组合设置复杂性与可靠性。
• 精简配置技术的潜在问题。
• 不同RAID级别和文件系统（如ZFS、Btrfs）在数据保护和性能上的优劣。
• 使用缓存与分层技术时的性能与可靠性权衡。

44698754.article_content:
Since the inception of
solid-state drives
(SSDs), there has been a choice
to make—either use SSDs for vastly superior speeds, especially with
non-sequential read and writes (“random I/O”), or use legacy spinning
rust
hard disk drives
(HDDs) for cheaper storage that’s a bit slow for
sequential I/O
1
and
painfully
slow for random I/O.
The idea of caching frequently used data on SSDs and storing the rest on HDDs is
nothing new—
solid-state hybrid drives
(SSHDs) embodied this idea in
hardware form, while filesystems like
ZFS
support using SSDs
as
L2ARC
. However, with
the falling price of SSDs, this no longer makes sense outside of niche scenarios
with very large amounts of storage. For example, I have not needed to use HDDs
in my PC for many years at this point, since all my data easily fits on an SSD.
One of the scenarios in which this makes sense is for
the mirrors
I host
at home. Oftentimes, a project will require hundreds of gigabytes of data to be
mirrored just in case anyone needs it, but only a few files are frequently
accessed and could be cached on SSDs for fast access
2
. Similarly, I have
many LLMs locally with
Ollama
, but there are only a few I use very
frequently. The frequently used ones can be cached while the rest can be loaded
slowly from HDD when needed.
While ZFS may seem like the obvious option here, due to Linux compatibility
issues with ZFS
mentioned previously
, I decided to use
Linux’s
Logical Volume Manager (LVM)
instead for this task to save myself
some headache. To ensure reliable storage in the event of HDD failures, I am
running the HDDs in
RAID 1
with Linux’s
mdadm
software RAID.
This post documents how to build such a cached RAID array and explores some
considerations when building reliable and fast storage.
Table of contents
Why use LVM cache?
A quick introduction to LVM
The hardware setup
Why use RAID 1 on HDDs?
Setting up RAID 1 with
mdadm
Creating the SSD cache partition
Creating a new volume group
Creating the cached LV
Creating a filesystem
Mounting the new filesystem
Monitoring
Conclusion
Why use LVM cache?
There are several alternative block device caching solutions on Linux, such as:
bcache
: a built-in Linux kernel module that does similar caching
as LVM. I don’t like the way it’s set up by owning the entire block device and
non-persistent sysfs configurations, compared to LVM remembering all the
configuration options, nor do I enjoy hearing about all the reports of bcache
corrupting data; and
EnhanceIO
: an old kernel module that does something similar to
bcache and LVM cache, but hasn’t been maintained for over a decade.
Since I am very familiar with LVM and have already used it for other reasons, I
opted to use LVM for this exercise as well.
A quick introduction to LVM
If you aren’t familiar with LVM, we’ll need to first introduce some concepts, or
none of the LVM portions of this post will make any sense.
First, we’ll need to introduce block devices, which are just devices with a
fixed number of blocks that can be read at any offset. HDDs and SSDs show up as
block devices, such
/dev/sda
. They can be partitioned into multiple pieces,
showing up as smaller block devices such as
/dev/sda1
, the first partition on
/dev/sda
. Filesystems can be created directly on block devices, but these
block devices can also be used with more advanced things like RAID and LVM.
LVM is a volume manager that allows you to create logical volumes that can be
expanded much more easily than regular partitions. In LVM, there are three major
entity types:
Physical volumes (PVs)
: block devices that are used as the underlying
storage for LVM;
Logical volumes (LVs)
: block devices that are presented by LVM, stored on
one or more PVs; and
Volume groups (VGs)
: a group of PVs on which LVs can be created.
LVs can be used just like partitions to store files, with the flexibility of
being able to expand them at will while they are
actively being accessed
,
without having to be contiguous like real partitions.
There are more advanced LV types, such as thin pools, which doesn’t allocate
space for LVs until they are actually used to store data, and cached volumes,
which this post is about.
The hardware
For the purposes of this post, we will assume that there are two SATA HDDs (
4 TB each in my case), available as block devices
/dev/sda
and
/dev/sdb
:
$
lsblk
NAME               MAJ:MIN RM   SIZE RO TYPE  MOUNTPOINTS
sda                  8:0    0   3.6T  0 disk
sdb                  8:16   0   3.6T  0 disk
...
Warning
: before copying any commands, ensure that you are operating on the
correct device. There is no undo button for most of the commands in this post,
so be very careful lest you destroy your precious data! When in doubt, run
lsblk
to double check!
We’ll also assume that the SSD is
/dev/nvme0n1
3
(2 TB in my case),
and we will allocate 100 GiB of it as the cache by creating a partition.

Why use RAID 1 on HDDs?
Mechanical HDDs, like everything mechanical,

data.title: A low power 1U Raspberry Pi cluster server for inexpensive colocation (2021)
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个基于Raspberry Pi的低功耗1U集群服务器项目，旨在以低成本实现服务器托管。项目设计目标是在1A @ 120V的功率限制内，最大化计算能力、存储和性价比。服务器使用Supermicro 1U机箱，内含5个Raspberry Pi 4b作为单板计算机，每个配备Geekworm外壳和Kingston A400 M.2 SSD用于存储。网络部分使用NETGEAR 8口千兆交换机，并通过继电器模块实现远程电源管理。项目总成本约800美元，功耗在空闲时为36-48W，负载时为43.2-50.4W，符合托管服务商的功率限制。文章还详细列出了硬件组装、软件设置及功耗测量方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Raspberry Pi服务器集群项目的实用性、技术细节及替代方案

不同观点：
• 项目作者[postpawl]认为，项目已有4年历史，目前可能使用Mac minis或mini PC更为合适。他也提到廉价托管服务存在安全隐患，例如IP冲突问题。此外，托管公司破产后硬件被归还，表明技术故障风险高。
• [mvip]推荐参考Mythic Beasts的做法，他们将大量Raspberry Pi装入机架，并托管Raspberry Pi官网，提供了实际案例和图片链接。
• [Catbert59]建议使用Intel n100/n150/n305系列设备，特别是n100，因其无活动部件更稳定，但对于n150及以上需要注意主动散热问题。
• [nateb2022]认为该项目的性价比不高，相比之下Hetzner等提供商的服务器配置更高、费用更低，且可以通过eBay淘零件组装更好的服务器。
• [procaryote]提出可以通过直接从继电器供电到Pi的电源引脚来节省USB适配器，并建议添加串行控制台和电源按钮功能，还提到可以使用Pi5和M2板来优化设计。
• [rbanffy]提到许多集群板允许插入计算模块板，并自带开关，可以提供更密集的系统，但制作新板需要大量工作，且涉及复杂的网络设计。
• [bullen]分享了自己构建的集群，使用自托管和家庭光纤，节省空间并实现静音散热，同时提到Raspberry 5和3588发热较高。
• [omarqureshi]描述了自己的类似设置，使用Pi 5和PoE Hats，效果良好且无需额外电源，但遇到PoE Hats风扇问题。

补充讨论：
• [hawk_]询问任意供应商的托管意义，表明对托管应用场景的困惑。
• [dnemmers]担心项目硬件在运输中难以保持完整，但认为在家中使用可能没问题。
• [asteroidburger]指出项目中16GB DDR4内存和1.2TB存储在多个节点间分配，性能不足。
• [arnon]对项目创意表示认可，但认为其难以持久运行。
• [crinkly]提到托管公司对硬件要求严格，且微型集群的IPv4成本问题是个挑战，但认为该项目可能适合IPv6集群。

争议焦点：
• 项目的实用性和性价比受到质疑，尤其是与传统托管服务和硬件方案对比时。

Raspberry Pi 1U Server
There are server colocation providers that allow hosting a 1U server for as low as $30/month, but there's a catch: There are restrictions on power usage (1A @ 120v max, for example) because they're expecting small and power-efficient network equipment like firewalls.
This repo is about designing a server that fits within the 1U space and 1A @ 120v power constraint while maximizing computing power, storage, and value.

44660219.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个基于Raspberry Pi的低功耗1U集群服务器项目，旨在以低成本实现服务器托管。项目设计目标是在1A @ 120V的功率限制内，最大化计算能力、存储和性价比。服务器使用Supermicro 1U机箱，内含5个Raspberry Pi 4b作为单板计算机，每个配备Geekworm外壳和Kingston A400 M.2 SSD用于存储。网络部分使用NETGEAR 8口千兆交换机，并通过继电器模块实现远程电源管理。项目总成本约800美元，功耗在空闲时为36-48W，负载时为43.2-50.4W，符合托管服务商的功率限制。文章还详细列出了硬件组装、软件设置及功耗测量方法。
44660219.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Raspberry Pi服务器集群项目的实用性、技术细节及替代方案

不同观点：
• 项目作者[postpawl]认为，项目已有4年历史，目前可能使用Mac minis或mini PC更为合适。他也提到廉价托管服务存在安全隐患，例如IP冲突问题。此外，托管公司破产后硬件被归还，表明技术故障风险高。
• [mvip]推荐参考Mythic Beasts的做法，他们将大量Raspberry Pi装入机架，并托管Raspberry Pi官网，提供了实际案例和图片链接。
• [Catbert59]建议使用Intel n100/n150/n305系列设备，特别是n100，因其无活动部件更稳定，但对于n150及以上需要注意主动散热问题。
• [nateb2022]认为该项目的性价比不高，相比之下Hetzner等提供商的服务器配置更高、费用更低，且可以通过eBay淘零件组装更好的服务器。
• [procaryote]提出可以通过直接从继电器供电到Pi的电源引脚来节省USB适配器，并建议添加串行控制台和电源按钮功能，还提到可以使用Pi5和M2板来优化设计。
• [rbanffy]提到许多集群板允许插入计算模块板，并自带开关，可以提供更密集的系统，但制作新板需要大量工作，且涉及复杂的网络设计。
• [bullen]分享了自己构建的集群，使用自托管和家庭光纤，节省空间并实现静音散热，同时提到Raspberry 5和3588发热较高。
• [omarqureshi]描述了自己的类似设置，使用Pi 5和PoE Hats，效果良好且无需额外电源，但遇到PoE Hats风扇问题。

补充讨论：
• [hawk_]询问任意供应商的托管意义，表明对托管应用场景的困惑。
• [dnemmers]担心项目硬件在运输中难以保持完整，但认为在家中使用可能没问题。
• [asteroidburger]指出项目中16GB DDR4内存和1.2TB存储在多个节点间分配，性能不足。
• [arnon]对项目创意表示认可，但认为其难以持久运行。
• [crinkly]提到托管公司对硬件要求严格，且微型集群的IPv4成本问题是个挑战，但认为该项目可能适合IPv6集群。

争议焦点：
• 项目的实用性和性价比受到质疑，尤其是与传统托管服务和硬件方案对比时。

data.title: 16colo.rs: ANSI/ASCII art archive
data.author: debo_
data.article_summary: Sixteen Colors是一个在线存档平台，专门收集ANSI和ASCII艺术包（artpacks）。这些艺术作品最初是为计算机文本模式控制台设计的，在20世纪90年代随着拨号 bulletin board systems (BBS) 的兴起而流行。艺术家们组成团体，按月发布艺术包，并因团体间的竞争而促进了这一活动的发展。尽管随着互联网的兴起，BBS和ANSI/ASCII艺术的需求和兴趣逐渐减少，但仍有艺术家继续创作。Sixteen Colors作为一个公共档案库，旨在保存这些艺术包，并提供上传、协作、搜索和聊天等功能，以支持这一艺术形式的发展和交流。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕ASCII/ANSI艺术及其相关怀旧情绪的讨论

不同观点：
• saidinesh5和majkinetor表达了对ASCII艺术及键盘生成音乐（keygen music）的怀旧情感，分享了相关的资源链接。
• sen提到自己通过在终端打开时随机加载收集的.ANS文件，重温连接BBS的怀旧感受。
• debo_推荐使用Gemini浏览器访问一个包含50k+ ANSI/ASCII图像的网站，模拟通过调制解调器下载的体验。
• ilaksh提供了在Linux上播放ANSI文件的程序`durdraw`的信息，并推荐了Perfect DOS VGA 437字体，但指出该程序不会在播放后保留图像。
• xyst对IRC客户端BitchX未包含ASCII艺术表示遗憾，并提供了维基百科链接。
• ptek提到在无法负担PS1或电脑配置较差时，ASCII艺术是一种替代娱乐方式，并分享了相关资源。
• greeniskool分享了一个“Bad Apple”的ANSI艺术转换版本链接。

补充讨论：
• ssilver询问了用于绘制这些艺术作品的常用编辑器，这一问题未得到直接回答。
• kls0e提到了一位叫roy sparks的艺术家，其作品带来了极大的喜悦。
• yowayb分享了使用AI工具Grok生成ANSI艺术的失败尝试，输出结果不如预期，指出了AI生成艺术的局限性。

争议焦点：
• 讨论中并无明显争议，但yowayb的评论暗示了对AI生成艺术质量的不满，相对于怀旧的手工艺术，AI生成的结果显得不够理想。

About Sixteen Colors:
Sixteen Colors is an online archive for ANSI and ASCII artpacks. The artform was originally intended for display on computer textmode consoles. It gained popularity in
the early nineties with the rise of dial-up Bulletin Board Systems (BBS).
At one point artists started to group together and release their work in collections released monthly, these collection are called artpacks. Rivalry resulted in fierce
competition between these artgroups which only boosted activity.
ACiD
and
iCE
are examples of early prominent groups.
The rise of the Internet in the late nineties started the decline of BBS's and thus also the need and interest for ANSI/ASCII art. And although the need has almost vanished, still today artists are producing artpacks in collectives. Sixteen Colors aims to collect these artpacks as an archive in the public interest.
Want to know more? A good starting point is
THE ART OF WAREZ
is a short-film about the origins and history of the ANSI art scene.

data.title: Janet: Lightweight, Expressive, Modern Lisp
data.author: veqq
data.article_summary: Janet是一个功能性和命令式编程语言，核心部分不到1MB，可运行于Windows、Linux、macOS、BSD等系统，易于移植。它既可作为系统脚本语言，也可嵌入其他程序中使用，适用于快速原型设计和动态系统开发。Janet使用标准C99编写，支持线程、网络、事件循环、C语言直接互操作等功能，并附带REPL和调试器。其核心库包含500多个函数和宏，支持将项目导出为独立可执行文件。Janet还提供诸如PEG等高级特性，并可通过jpm工具安装包，如HTTP服务器、Web开发框架、JSON解析器等库。社区和文档资源丰富，支持多种编辑器和平台。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lisp语言及其变种（如Janet）的开发体验、生态系统、性能和工具支持

不同观点：
• **uvas_pasas_per**：认为Lisp的语法风格`(fun a b c)`在IDE自动补全方面不如面向对象语言的`.fun(b, c)`直观。开发者需要频繁考虑函数签名，这增加了认知负担。他希望找到一种方法，让编辑和自动补全更顺畅。
• **zelphirkalt**：关注Janet等Lisp变种的生态系统，尤其是库的支持。他提到GNU Guile和Racket有丰富的库，但对Janet的库（如web服务器、JSON解析器、数据结构等）表示担忧。此外，他还强调了可重现性和学习资源的匮乏。
• **dusted**：对Lisp的简洁语法表示欣赏，但尚未实现完整的函数功能，且项目较为混乱，仅为解释型。
• **dmpk2k**：询问Janet是否有原生编译器和类型系统，能否达到SBCL的性能水平，同时希望有更小的镜像尺寸。
• **bjoli**：质疑Janet的独特性，认为它只是Scheme的变种，没有足够的理由从Guile切换到Janet。
• **rich_sasha**：希望有一个决策树来帮助选择合适的Lisp变种（如CL, Scheme, Racket, Clojure, Janet）。
• **NeutralForest**：指出Janet的工具支持不足，尤其是在IDE中与REPL交互开发和调试的工具较少。
• **nemoniac**：对Janet文档中的3SUM问题示例提出质疑，认为其并未解决标准的3SUM问题，并提供了Common Lisp的解决方案。
• **firemelt**：表示无法忍受Lisp的语法噪音。
• **raydenvm**：询问Janet是否有已知的商业用例。
• **revskill**：质疑Janet如何处理异步操作（async/await）。
• **WillAdams**：遗憾于Janet缺乏GUI库，并希望能够编译成独立程序或JavaScript以托管在Github页面上。

补充讨论：
• Janet的生态系统和库支持是一个主要关注点，尤其是对于想要快速开始项目而不必从头构建基础工具的开发者。
• 性能方面，开发者对Janet是否能达到SBCL的性能水平表示关注。
• 工具和IDE支持也是一个重要问题，尤其是自动补全、交互式开发和调试的支持。
• 一些开发者对Lisp语法在IDE中的表现提出改进建议，而另一些开发者则对语法本身表示不满。
• 关于Janet的独特性和是否有足够的理由从其他Lisp变种切换过来，也存在一定争议。

争议焦点：
• Janet是否具备足够的库和工具支持以满足实际项目需求。
• Lisp语法在IDE中的自动补全和开发体验问题。
• Janet文档中的3SUM问题示例是否准确。

44698185.article_content:
Janet Language
Janet is a functional and imperative programming language. It runs on Windows, Linux,
macOS, BSDs, and should run on other systems with some porting. The entire language (core library,
interpreter, compiler, assembler, PEG) is less than 1MB. You can also add Janet scripting
to an application by embedding a single C source file and a single header.
Download
Source
Documentation
Core API
Forum
Use Cases
Janet makes a good system scripting language, or a language to embed in other programs.  Janet also can be used for rapid prototyping, dynamic systems, and other domains
where dynamic languages shine. Implemented mostly in standard C99, Janet runs on Windows, Linux and macOS.
The few features that are not standard C (dynamic library loading, compiler specific optimizations),
are fairly straightforward. Janet can be easily ported to new platforms. While Janet is embeddable, it comes with a bit more out of the box than many other such easily embeddable languages
such as threading, networking, an event loop, subprocess handling, regex-like library called PEG, and more.
Features
Minimal setup - one binary and you are good to go!
Builtin support for threads, networking, and an event loop

44698185.article_summary: Janet是一个功能性和命令式编程语言，核心部分不到1MB，可运行于Windows、Linux、macOS、BSD等系统，易于移植。它既可作为系统脚本语言，也可嵌入其他程序中使用，适用于快速原型设计和动态系统开发。Janet使用标准C99编写，支持线程、网络、事件循环、C语言直接互操作等功能，并附带REPL和调试器。其核心库包含500多个函数和宏，支持将项目导出为独立可执行文件。Janet还提供诸如PEG等高级特性，并可通过jpm工具安装包，如HTTP服务器、Web开发框架、JSON解析器等库。社区和文档资源丰富，支持多种编辑器和平台。

主要讨论点：Lisp语言及其变种（如Janet）的开发体验、生态系统、性能和工具支持

不同观点：
• **uvas_pasas_per**：认为Lisp的语法风格`(fun a b c)`在IDE自动补全方面不如面向对象语言的`.fun(b, c)`直观。开发者需要频繁考虑函数签名，这增加了认知负担。他希望找到一种方法，让编辑和自动补全更顺畅。
• **zelphirkalt**：关注Janet等Lisp变种的生态系统，尤其是库的支持。他提到GNU Guile和Racket有丰富的库，但对Janet的库（如web服务器、JSON解析器、数据结构等）表示担忧。此外，他还强调了可重现性和学习资源的匮乏。
• **dusted**：对Lisp的简洁语法表示欣赏，但尚未实现完整的函数功能，且项目较为混乱，仅为解释型。
• **dmpk2k**：询问Janet是否有原生编译器和类型系统，能否达到SBCL的性能水平，同时希望有更小的镜像尺寸。
• **bjoli**：质疑Janet的独特性，认为它只是Scheme的变种，没有足够的理由从Guile切换到Janet。
• **rich_sasha**：希望有一个决策树来帮助选择合适的Lisp变种（如CL, Scheme, Racket, Clojure, Janet）。

• **firemelt**：表示无法忍受Lisp的语法噪音。
• **raydenvm**：询问Janet是否有已知的商业用例。

• 关于Janet的独特性和是否有足够的理由从其他Lisp变种切换过来，也存在一定争议。

争议焦点：
• Janet是否具备足够的库和工具支持以满足实际项目需求。
• Lisp语法在IDE中的自动补全和开发体验问题。
• Janet文档中的3SUM问题示例是否准确。

data.title: Hierarchical Reasoning Model
data.author: hansmayer
data.article_summary: 本文提出了一种分层推理模型（Hierarchical Reasoning Model, HRM），旨在解决当前大型语言模型在处理复杂目标导向任务时的不足。HRM受人脑分层和多时间尺度处理的启发，通过两个相互依赖的递归模块实现深度计算：负责缓慢抽象规划的高层模块和处理快速详细计算的低层模块。HRM在仅有2700万参数的情况下，使用1000个训练样本即可在复杂推理任务中取得优异表现，无需预训练或链式思考（CoT）数据。该模型在抽象与推理数据集（ARC）上超越了更大的模型，展示了其在通用计算和推理系统中的潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HRM模型的性能、原理及其潜在应用和争议

不同观点：
• **积极评价**：
   - [cs702] 认为HRM模型在多个复杂任务（如Sudoku和迷宫问题）上表现出色，尤其在不使用预训练和大量数据的情况下，超过了当前最先进的CoT方法。
   - [topspin] 强调HRM模型的层次推理机制类似于人脑的认知模式，特别是通过自适应停止策略实现“快慢思考”的机制，并认为这种多模块合作是实现AGI的潜在途径。
   - [advael] 对HRM模型使用递归模块增强注意力模型的方法表示赞赏，认为这是未来研究的一个有前景的方向。

• **与认知科学理论的关联**：
   - [SubiculumCode] 从认知心理学角度出发，认为HRM模型与“模糊痕迹理论”相吻合，该理论主张记忆和认知在不同层次上运作，这与HRM的多层次推理机制相似。

• **怀疑与批评**：
   - [JonathanRaines] 对HRM模型的结果表示怀疑，指出该研究尚未经过同行评审，且结果部分缺乏评估细节，实际性能可能不如文中声称的那样优越。
   - [malcontented] 虽然不否认HRM模型的创新性，但对其与CoT模型的比较提出质疑，认为HRM模型更像是一个特定问题的解题器，而非通用的任务解决者。

• **潜在应用与扩展**：
   - [lispitillo] 提出HRM模型与MoE（专家混合模型）结合的可能性，并预测这种结合可能在短时间内实现，但指出HRM模型当前的应用场景有限，缺乏对未来应用的讨论。
   - [OgsyedIE] 认为HRM模型的嵌套结构可以与MoE系统结合，创造出在效率和质量上都有新突破的模型。
   - [camphy] 关注HRM模型在模糊推理场景中的应用潜力，认为目前模型在定义明确的问题空间（如Sudoku）上表现优异，但对其在更复杂环境中的表现存疑。

• **幽默与调侃**：
   - [0x000xca0xfe] 开玩笑地提到HRM模型可能终结CAPTCHA验证码。
   - [belter] 质疑HRM模型是否只是ReAct、Chain-of-Thought和结构化规划的变种。
   - [electroglyph] 简单直接地问“但它能扩展吗？”

补充讨论：
• **实验验证需求**：
   - [nowittyusername] 表示虽然HRM模型的概念听起来合理，但需要第三方验证其实际效果。
   - [smokel] 计划通过GitHub仓库亲自验证HRM模型的效果，并对其无需预训练即可解决规则学习问题表示惊讶。

争议焦点：HRM模型的实际性能、与CoT模型的比较以及其在不同场景中的通用性和扩展性。

Title:
Hierarchical Reasoning Model
Authors:
Guan Wang
,
Jin Li

View a PDF of the paper titled Hierarchical Reasoning Model, by Guan Wang and 8 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Reasoning, the process of devising and executing complex goal-oriented action sequences, remains a critical challenge in AI. Current large language models (LLMs) primarily employ Chain-of-Thought (CoT) techniques, which suffer from brittle task decomposition, extensive data requirements, and high latency. Inspired by the hierarchical and multi-timescale processing in the human brain, we propose the Hierarchical Reasoning Model (HRM), a novel recurrent architecture that attains significant computational depth while maintaining both training stability and efficiency. HRM executes sequential reasoning tasks in a single forward pass without explicit supervision of the intermediate process, through two interdependent recurrent modules: a high-level module responsible for slow, abstract planning, and a low-level module handling rapid, detailed computations. With only 27 million parameters, HRM achieves exceptional performance on complex reasoning tasks using only 1000 training samples. The model operates without pre-training or CoT data, yet achieves nearly perfect performance on challenging tasks including complex Sudoku puzzles and optimal path finding in large mazes. Furthermore, HRM outperforms much larger models with significantly longer context windows on the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC), a key benchmark for measuring artificial general intelligence capabilities. These results underscore HRM's potential as a transformative advancement toward universal computation and general-purpose reasoning systems.

data.title: Linux on Snapdragon X Elite: Linaro and Tuxedo Pave the Way for ARM64 Laptops
data.author: MarcusE1W
data.article_summary: 在2025年Linaro Connect大会上，Linaro与TUXEDO Computers展示了采用Snapdragon X Elite SoC的ARM64 Linux笔记本原型，标志着Linux对Snapdragon设备支持的重大进展。尽管Windows on Arm是这些设备的主要操作系统，但Linaro和Qualcomm的合作推动了Linux在多款ARM64笔记本上的支持，包括Lenovo、Dell、HP等品牌的设备。当前Linux内核6.15版已支持多款商用笔记本，功能涵盖GPU加速、外接显示、音频、摄像头、Wi-Fi等方面。尽管Linux在ARM64笔记本上的体验尚不及x86笔记本，但Ubuntu和Fedora等发行版正逐步增加支持。TUXEDO Computers承诺推出预装Linux的Qualcomm笔记本，显示出Linux在ARM架构桌面应用的成熟潜力。总体而言，Linux对Snapdragon笔记本的支持正稳步推进，为用户提供了更多选择和创新机会。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux在笔记本上的支持情况，特别是Tuxedo品牌的笔记本、ARM架构设备以及整体移动计算领域的现状和未来发展。

不同观点：
• **对Tuxedo笔记本的失望**：[pentamassiv] 表示Tuxedo笔记本未兑现承诺，如fwupd支持、上游驱动以及coreboot支持都未实现。内核开发者曾考虑将其列入黑名单。此外，维修困难且费用高，整体体验不佳。
• **对苹果设备的不满**：[fb03] 表达了对当前移动计算领域的不满，特别是对苹果设备和Windows系统的依赖。虽然硬件强大，但软件支持不足，尤其是Snapdragon处理器上的Linux支持滞后。

At Linaro Connect 2025 Linaro, thanks to its work within the Qualcomm ecosystem, and TUXEDO Computers, showcased an off-the-shelf prototype ARM64 Linux laptop using the Snapdragon X Elite SoC, demonstrating progress in enabling Linux on Snapdragon devices to meet the increasing demand for ARM computing.
But wait! This is just the tip of the iceberg of a long journey!
Advancements in Linux Support for Snapdragon X Elite:
Over the past year, substantial progress has been made in integrating Linux support for Snapdragon X Elite laptops.
Qualcomm and many laptop vendors worked together to bring to market a new family of Snapdragon-powered personal computers. This new processor family ticks all the boxes for powerful and productive machines, and the collaboration with Microsoft brought the support for Windows on Arm on these devices as the main operating system (which Linaro has
contributed to as well
).
Unfortunately, like Apple computers, there is no native out-of-the-box Linux support.
The effort from Qualcomm and Linaro has been crucial to bring a functional Linux to the new family of ARM64-powered laptops.
The engineering experts from Qualcomm, Linaro and the kernel community have made a stable Linux experience possible across many Qualcomm processors, including the newer Snapdragon X Elite.
But we are still missing pre-installed Linux laptops. In the x86 processor-based laptop market, many vendors now offer Linux options.
State of the art:
Where are we now with the Linux support on these Snapdragon laptops?
A year after the processor announcement, the current Linux Kernel 6.15 already supports many commercial laptops:
Lenovo Yoga 7x
Lenovo ThinkPad T14s Gen 6
Dell XPS 13
Asus Vivobook S15
HP Omnibook x14
Microsoft Surface 13/15
The enablement wouldn’t have been possible without the collaboration between Linaro, Qualcomm, the community, and the laptop vendors.
During the last few years, Linaro engineers have contributed to many improvements in terms of functionalities and use cases, including:
GPU and 2D/3D acceleration
External display output (USB-C DP altmode)
USB enablement
Audio support
Software camera support
Thermal management
Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/Modem
Suspend/resume
Contact Us
to know more.
Currently, the Linux experience on ARM64 laptops lags behind Windows on the same hardware and Linux on x86 laptops. Linaro’s goal is to enhance the out-of-the-box experience, reliability, and overall user experience on Qualcomm-powered laptops running popular Linux distributions, such as Debian and Fedora, by addressing fundamental issues.
Watch the Linux ARM64 Compute Laptops BoF discussion at Linaro Connect 2025
Thanks to the changes available in the kernel, Ubuntu community has released an installable Concept Distro for Ubuntu 24.10 and now Canonical is adding ARM64 Laptops
support for Ubuntu 25.04 distro
and also
Fedora is working on it
.
In other words, the development progress is going in the right direction, distro support is on its way and many people are starting to drive these devices with Linux daily.
TUXEDO Computers’ Commitment to Linux on ARM:
The integration of Linux on Qualcomm laptops signifies more than just a technical milestone. It has the potential to create a positive impact on the global technology ecosystem and the wider market.
This is what the folks at
TUXEDO Computers
are putting their bets on, a full-fledged laptop with one of the latest and innovative ARM64 processors with Linux. The promise and the commitment from TUXEDO to release a Qualcomm Laptop with pre-installed Linux is a living fact that this operating system is mature enough for desktop use on these devices.
Tuxedo directly contacted us for help for technical support to bring up the missing bits on the device, and they sent us two prototypes to develop on. Collaboration between experts from both companies successfully enabled Linux installation and the proper functioning of many features on this device.
The unique nature of this case study and its growing interest create new opportunities for developers, businesses, and consumers who require Linux in their Snapdragon X Series family products, paving the way for increased choice and innovation in the ARM64-based laptop space and beyond.

While we are still in the development phase, we can confidently say that users can look forward to long battery

data.title: Implementing dynamic scope for Fennel and Lua
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了在Fennel和Lua中实现动态作用域（dynamic scoping）的方法。Lua虚拟机不支持动态作用域，Fennel也没有类似Clojure的`Var`概念。然而，通过使用Lua的`debug`库，可以模拟Clojure等Lisp语言中的动态作用域。作者希望实现一个更符合Lisp习惯的动态作用域机制，而不是通过显式引用变量名的方式。

文章首先解释了词法作用域（lexical scoping）和动态作用域的区别。词法作用域下，变量仅在其定义的代码块内有效；而动态作用域允许变量在特定动态范围内像全局变量一样被访问。作者通过一个代码重构的例子展示了词法作用域的局限性，并对比了Clojure中使用`binding`实现动态作用域的方法。

最后，作者提到可以参考Leafo的指南来实现这一特性，并计划在fennel-cljlib项目中继续推进这一工作。

• **对动态绑定的兴趣与疑虑**：tikotus提到他对**动态绑定**的概念很感兴趣，尤其是在为游戏开发设计的脚本语言中。但他对动态绑定在协程中的表现存在疑问，似乎不确定动态绑定如何在协程环境中有效工作。

• **可预测性与意外行为**：tikotus强调了使用隐式上下文对象的一个优点，即它能够减少使用中的“意外”。这表明他可能认为动态绑定在某些场景下，尤其是涉及协程时，可能会引入不易察觉的复杂性或不可预测性。

• **协程的支持**：tikotus特别提到自己是**协程的频繁使用者**，因此他关注的是哪种方法能更好地支持协程操作。他似乎认为隐式上下文对象在这方面更具优势。

• **适用场景的考虑**：tikotus在动态绑定和隐式上下文对象之间摇摆不定，表明他仍在评估哪种方法能更好地满足其脚本语言的具体需求，尤其是针对游戏开发的特殊场景。

争议焦点：动态绑定在协程环境下的适用性和可预测性是争议的核心，tikotus显然对这一点存在疑虑。

44663887.article_content:
Implementing dynamic scope for Fennel and Lua
Mon, Jun 9, 2025
@programming
lua
fennel
clojure
~11 minutes read
I’m continuing my work on
fennel-cljlib
, my port of
clojure.core
and some other core libraries, focusing on porting missing functions and features to it.
One such feature, which I sometimes miss in Lua and Fennel, is
dynamic binding
.
The Lua VM doesn’t provide dynamic scoping as a language feature, and Fennel itself doesn’t introduce any concepts like Clojure’s
Var
.
However, we can still implement dynamic scoping that works similarly to Clojure and other Lisps using the
debug
library.
Most of the ideas are based on information from the
guides
at
leafo.net
.
There’s even a
“Dynamic scoping in Lua”
guide that implements a slightly different version of this feature, requiring variables to be referenced by name via
dynamic("var_name")
call.
While this approach is feasible, I wanted something more in line with how other Lisps work, so let’s explore advancing it further.
Luckily for us, Leafo already has all the necessary guides!
But first things first.
I wanted to delay working on dynamic scoping as much as possible because it is a feature that’s hard to get right.
I already have some experience with implementing dynamic scoping for one of my older libraries that implemented a
condition system
from Common Lisp in Fennel.
This library, however, required special syntax to access all of the dynamically bound symbols and thus did not actually require anything fancy for it to work.
So what does dynamic binding/scoping mean in a language?
If you know about lexical and dynamic scoping and wish to skip this tangent, feel free to
do so
.
In short, lexically scoped variables exist only where their lexical scope allows them to.
For example, a variable defined in a block of code will only exist in that block because it is its lexical scope.
When working with languages that have higher-order functions, I often find myself in a situation where I want to refactor some code that uses anonymous functions by moving them out and giving them a name.
Sometimes it’s possible; sometimes it’s not.
For example, imagine I wanted to move out this function from
map
:
(
fn
some-func
[
messages
]
(
let
[
extra-data
(
other-func
)]
(
map
(
fn
[
message
]
(
do-stuff
message
extra-data
))
messages
)))
If I were to do so, we would have a problem:
(
fn
process-message
[
message
]
;; oops, extra-data is now an unknown variable
(
do-stuff
message
extra-data
))
(
fn
some-func
[
messages
]
(
let
[
extra-data
(
other-func
)]
(
map
process-message
messages
)))
So
extra-data
is bound lexically, and thus if we look at the lexical scope of the
process-messages
function, we’ll see that it tries to use
extra-data
while it’s not defined there.
If
extra-data
were a global variable, it wouldn’t be problematic, but it is a local variable with a lexical scope.
We could move the entire
let
that binds
extra-data
to the result of calling
other-func
, but let’s say we don’t want to call it on each iteration of a
map
because it’s slow and will do the same work repeatedly.
So, what are our options here?
Well, we can make it a closure!
(
fn
make-message-processor
[
extra-data
]
(
fn
process-message
[
message
]
(
do-stuff
message
extra-data
)))
(
fn
some-func
[
messages
]
(
let
[
extra-data
(
other-func
)]
(
map
(
make-message-processor
extra-data
)
messages
)))
Now, we pass
extra-data
only once to the
make-message-processor
function, and it returns a function that has this variable stored in a closure.
However, this is still a lexical scope because, as you can see,
extra-data
is present there.
In a language that uses dynamic scoping, this could be a whole different story.
Let’s look at Clojure; although I wouldn’t recommend doing it this way, it is possible to do it this way
1
:
(
defn
process-message
[
message
]
(
do-stuff
message
extra-data
))
(
defn
some-func
[
messages
]
(
binding
[
extra-data
(
other-func
)]
(
mapv
process-message
messages
)))
Here, I assume that
extra-data
is a dynamic variable that obeys the rules of dynamic scoping.
The
binding
call introduces a dynamic scope within which
extra-data
is set to the value of
(other-func)
.
It acts more like a scoped global variable, or at least you can think of it that way.
To introduce a dynamic scope, Clojure uses
binding
.
Let’s look at it briefly:
(
defmacro
binding
"binding => var-symbol init-expr
Creates new bindings for the (already-existing) vars, with the
supplied initial values, executes the exprs in an implicit do, then
re-establishes the bindings that existed before.  The new bindings
are made in parallel (unlike let); all init-exprs are evaluated
before the vars are bound to their new values."
{
:added
"1.0"
}

bindings
&
body
]
(
assert-args
(
vector?
bindings
)
"a vector for its binding"
(
even?
(
count
bindings
))
"an even number of forms in binding vector"
)

[
var-ize
(

[
var-vals
]
(
loop
[

(
seq
var-vals
)]
(
if

(

(

(

data.title: 4k NASA employees opt to leave agency through deferred resignation program
data.author: ProAm
data.article_summary: 近4,000名NASA员工选择通过延迟辞职计划离开该机构，这将使NASA员工从18,000人减至14,000人。该计划是特朗普政府为减少联邦工作人员而推出的，预计将减少NASA约20%的员工。此外，特朗普政府还提议在2026财年将NASA预算削减约24%，但从近期通过的法律中，NASA到2032年将获得近100亿美元的额外资助，支持火星任务和重返月球计划。科学界和太空组织对预算削减提出批评，300多名现任和前任NASA员工联名致信，反对仓促且浪费的变革。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NASA人员削减及其影响

不同观点：
• **政治动机论**（[samrus], [yalogin], [EasyMark], [kubb]）：这部分评论认为，NASA的裁员是共和党或新政府通过削减联邦机构来推动私有化的策略，最终目的是为了将资源转移给私人企业或朋友公司，如Elon Musk的SpaceX。他们认为这是短视的资本主义行为，可能会对美国的科学和技术领导地位产生长期负面影响。

• **效率提升论**（[BobbyJo], [eagerpace], [almosthere]）：一些评论者认为，NASA需要改革，以变得更加高效和目标明确。他们主张将NASA拆分为更小、更专注的组织，并赋予其更具体、可衡量的目标。他们认为，目前的NASA因缺乏明确的目标和过时的技术（如SLS项目）而陷入困境，商业公司如SpaceX和Blue Origin可以提供更好的解决方案。

44699052.article_content:
NPR
Nearly 4,000 NASA employees opt to leave agency through deferred resignation program
Chandelis Duster
Jul. 26, 2025
MORE
Workers on scaffolding repaint the NASA logo near the top of the Vehicle Assembly Building at the Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Fla., May 2020.
Photo by
John Raoux
-
AP
Nearly 4,000 NASA employees have opted to leave the space agency through the Trump administration's deferred resignation program, NASA said on Saturday.
The cuts amount to an estimated 20% of NASA's workforce, and will reduce the agency from 18,000 to 14,000 employees, NASA spokesperson Cheryl Warner said in a statement shared with NPR. The total number includes the agency's loss of 500 other workers due to normal attrition, she said.
During a second round of the program, which closed at midnight Friday, 3,000 employees applied to leave the agency, Warner said, following the 870 employees that applied to leave during the first round.
The resignations follow the Trump administration's plan to reduce the federal workforce and implement cuts recommended by the
Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
.
NPR has reached out to the White House for comment.
It's unclear when the full reduction of the workforce will take effect, Warner said. NASA did not respond to NPR's questions about how the workforce cuts will affect the agency.
The administration has also proposed
decreasing NASA's budget
. A fiscal year 2026
budget request
released in May would reduce funding for the agency by about 24% (from nearly $25 billion to nearly $19 billion.) But the
House
and
Senate
are discussing recommendations that would keep funding for the agency around the current budget.
Concerning funding beyond the next fiscal year, however, the agency recently got a boost — reversing earlier proposals to retire some NASA programs. Trump's
One Big Beautiful Bill Act
that he signed into law earlier this month, allocates nearly $10 billion in additional funding for NASA through 2032, including backing for Mars missions and plans to return to the moon.
The White House's proposed budget cuts and changes at the agency have faced criticism from scientists and space organizations, including The Planetary Society, a nonprofit led by Bill Nye, "The Science Guy."
"The Planetary Society believes that a great nation deserves a great space program, one that reflects our national ideals and serves the public interest," the organization said about the White House budget proposal in May. "This proposal doesn't merely fall short — it actively rejects that promise, undermining the rare opportunity NASA provides to build unity at home and collaboration abroad through American leadership."
On Monday, more than 300 current and former NASA employees signed and sent a
letter
known as the "Voyager Declaration" to interim NASA administrator Sean Duffy, criticizing "rapid and wasteful changes" at the agency that they say include cuts to programs and research. They also urged Duffy to not implement the proposed cuts and said "they are not in the best interest of NASA."

data.title: Return of wolves to Yellowstone has led to a surge in aspen trees
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: 1995年，狼被重新引入黄石公园，之后公园内的杨树幼树开始显著增长，这是80年来首次出现新一代杨树。在狼被消灭后，马鹿数量失控，过度啃食植被，导致杨树无法生长。狼重新引入后，马鹿数量减少，杨树幼苗开始恢复。研究发现，许多区域出现了高大的杨树幼树，表明生态系统正在恢复。然而，虽然狼帮助了生态恢复，但野牛数量增加可能成为新的限制因素。杨树的恢复促进了生物多样性，支持了浆果灌木、昆虫、鸟类以及海狸等物种的生存。这显示了顶级捕食者对生态系统健康的重要性。

不同观点：

• pcmaffey强烈反对蒙大拿州提出的狼群捕猎新规，认为这些规定基于政治和利润而非科学，呼吁公众参与保护狼群。他们提供了具体的法规信息和评论建议。
• declan_roberts建议通过增加猎杀麋鹿许可证数量来控制麋鹿数量，而不是通过捕杀狼群，提出了另一种管理野生动物数量的方法。

• atentaten关注狼群重引入对山狮种群的影响，提出了生态平衡的复杂性问题。

44658323.article_content:
Wolves were reintroduced to Yellowstone in 1995, over 60 years after their eradication from the national park.
(Image credit: Photo by William Campbell/Sygma via Getty Images)
Yellowstone's wolves are helping a new generation of young aspen trees to grow tall and join the forest canopy — the first new generation of such trees in Yellowstone's northern range in 80 years.
Gray wolves (
Canis lupus
)
had disappeared from Yellowstone
National Park by 1930 following extensive habitat loss, human hunting and government eradication programs. Without these top predators, populations of elk (
Cervus canadensis
) grew unfettered. At their peak population, an estimated 18,000 elk ranged across the park, chomping on grasses and shrubs as well as the leaves, twigs and bark of trees like
quaking aspen
(
Populus tremuloides
). This stopped saplings from establishing themselves, and surveys in the 1990s found no aspen saplings.
"You had older trees, and then nothing underneath,"
Luke Painter
, an ecologist at Oregon State University and lead author of the new study, told Live Science.
You may like
Instead of 'de-extincting' dire wolves, scientists should use gene editing to protect living, endangered species
Colossal chief scientist clarifies de-extinction claim, while confirming its 'dire wolves' are 'grey wolves with 20 edits'
'This should not be published': Scientists cast doubt on study claiming trees 'talk' before solar eclipses
But when wolves were reintroduced in 1995, the picture began to change. As wolf numbers rose, the elk population in the park dropped sharply, and it is now down to about 2,000.
In the new study, published Tuesday (July 22) in the journal
Forest Ecology and Management
, Painter and his colleagues surveyed aspen stands — specific areas of the forest where these trees grow.
Related:
Reintroducing wolves to Yellowstone helped entire ecosystem thrive, 20-year study finds
The team returned to
three areas surveyed in 2012
to examine changes to aspen sapling numbers. Of the 87 aspen stands studied, a third had a large number of tall aspen saplings throughout, indicating the trees are healthy and growing. Another third of the stands had patches of tall saplings.
Sign up for the Live Science daily newsletter now
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands
Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors
"We're seeing significant new growth of young aspen and this is the first time that we've found it in our plots," Painter said. These are young aspen with a trunk greater than 2 inches (5 centimetres) in diameter at chest height — which haven't been seen there since the 1940s, he added.
"It doesn't mean that they're not going to get killed or die from something, but it's a pretty good indication that we're getting some new trees," Painter noted. "As they get bigger, they get more resilient."
Such trees are old enough to spread themselves, either by sending up new shoots from their roots a fair distance from the main tree, or via seed production, he said.
The researchers found tall aspen saplings in many of the sites studied.
(Image credit: Photo provided by Luke Painter, OSU College of Agricultural Sciences.)
However, while Yellowstone's quaking aspen are recovering, they aren't out of the woods just yet. The elk population has declined, but bison (
Bison bison
) numbers have increased in some areas in recent years.
Bison are a lot harder for wolves to take down
, said Painter, so increasing numbers of bison may be emerging as a new constraint on aspen in some areas.
Painter said that the variation in aspen recovery shows the effects of reintroducing a big predator to the top of the food chain, rather than to changes in the overall climate, for example.
The re-emergence of aspen has widespread effects, he told Live Science. "Aspen are a key species for biodiversity. The canopy is more open than it is with conifers and you get filtering light that creates a habitat that supports a lot of diversity of plants."
This means a boost to berry-producing shrubs, insects and birds and also species like beavers, because
the trees are a preferred food and building material for the semi- aquatic rodents
, along with the willows and cottonwoods that grow near to water in the region.
RELATED STORIES
—

—
Yellowstone National Park earthquake shakes hottest and oldest geothermal area
—
Giant coyote killed in southern Michigan turns out to be a gray wolf — despite the species vanishing from region 100 years ago
There are also hints that the number of bears and cougars in the region have increased since wolves were introduced, Painter said, but it's not clear why.
"The paper shows the important ecological benefits occurring from the restoration of wolves to Yellowstone National Park,"
Dominick Sprackl
